would_fix: Patterns > 'Open with gratitude and warmth': the sentence 'This move tells the introducer you recognize their effort, not as an aside in the closing, but as the primary reason for the message' invents a ranking ('the primary reason') the block never makes — the block (claim: open with thanks before logistics) says only the order of the reply, not that gratitude is 'the primary reason' for writing at all. Trim to the ordering fact.

Patterns > 'Provide a concrete scheduling mechanism': 'This accelerates agreement and removes barriers to booking' is an invented causal rationale (why handing over a link is good) that the block never states — the block only says hand over a link instead of trading open-ended availability, with no stated benefit/mechanism. Cut the sentence or attribute it as the drafter's own inference, not a sourced claim.

Form Conventions: 'The entire message should fit comfortably in 4-5 short sentences' is a fabricated number — no claim in the block quantifies message length at all. Delete; nothing in the source supports a sentence count.

Form Conventions: 'The referral-acceptance email compresses what would normally take multiple exchanges into one reply' is an invented generalization about email efficiency/exchange count not present in any of the 7 block claims. Cut or soften to 'handles both tasks in one message' (which the block does support via claim 1).

Form Conventions: 'Unlike [[email-internal-work-request-register|internal work requests]], which front status before the ask, a referral acceptance leads with gratitude...' asserts a specific structural claim about a DIFFERENT concept's article (internal-work-request register 'fronts status before the ask') that this concept block never states and isn't this block's source to verify. Remove the comparison or move it to that other article's own sourcing.

Form Conventions: 'Because the introducer is watching, you cannot defer thanks or hide the scheduling logistics in a follow-up' adds a prescriptive rule (no deferring to a follow-up email) not in the block's claim 1, which only says the reply must do double duty because the introducer is cc'd -- it says nothing about follow-up emails being forbidden. Trim to the block's actual scope.

Pitfalls > 'Vague closings': 'leave the new contact waiting for you to move next, prolonging the exchange and adding friction' is an invented mechanism/rationale for why vague closings are bad -- the block's claim 3 only contrasts a concrete next step against a vague 'I'll be in touch,' it doesn't explain the vague version 'prolongs the exchange' or 'adds friction.' Cut the added rationale.

Pitfalls > 'Hidden scheduling logistics': the entire pitfall ('Hiding the next step in a follow-up email... State the concrete mechanism -- the calendar link, the meeting room, the time window') is invented -- no block claim discusses hiding logistics in a follow-up, and 'the meeting room, the time window' are examples invented beyond the block's single example (a scheduling link). Delete this pitfall or replace with only what claim 5 supports (hand over a link, not open-ended availability).

Field Notes: the whole paragraph ('This email's efficiency comes from the three-party constraint... The warmth and concreteness work together -- openness to gratitude makes the logistics feel less transactional, and clear logistics make the gratitude feel genuine rather than obligatory') is speculative synthesis with no tie to any specific block claim -- it's the drafter's own theorizing about why the pattern works, not a sourced claim. Cut the section or reduce it to a plain restatement of claim 1's dual-duty point.

Overview paragraph states claim 1 (the dual-duty reply, because the introducer is cc'd and will see it) with no inline citation anywhere in the paragraph -- add [exemplar-referral-acknowledgment-email] at the end of the paragraph.

Pitfalls section (all three bullets, which restate claims 1/3/5/7 in the drafter's own words) carries zero inline citations -- add [exemplar-referral-acknowledgment-email] to each bullet or at minimum to the section.

Examples > 'Good' walkthrough: the explanatory line 'names the introducer by acknowledging her role' doesn't match its own example -- the reply is addressed 'Hi Sarah' and thanks Sarah 'for the introduction,' which only works if Sarah IS the introducer, yet the same sentence also has Sarah supplying 'your calendar' (the new contact's scheduling mechanism per claim 3/5). The example conflates the introducer and the new contact into one person, which the three-party premise (claim 1: introducer cc'd, separate from the new contact) does not support. Rewrite the example with two distinct people (an introducer thanked by name, a new contact whose calendar is booked) or clarify Sarah's single role.
